believe our current facilities are adequate to meet the requirements of our present operations.  </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="di70001_item_3._legal_proceedings."> </A>
<A NAME="toc_di70001_3"> </A></FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><B>  Item&nbsp;3.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;LEGAL PROCEEDINGS.    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>We are involved in a number of contingencies incidental to the normal conduct of our business including lawsuits, claims and environmental
contingencies. The outcome of these contingencies is inherently unpredictable. We believe that, in the aggregate, the outcome of all known contingencies including lawsuits, claims and environmental
contingencies will not have a material adverse effect on our financial statements; however, specific outcomes with respect to such
contingencies may be material to the financial statements of any particular period in which costs, if any, are recognized. Our assessment of the potential impact of the environmental contingencies is
subject to uncertainty due to the complex, ongoing and evolving process of investigation and remediation of such environmental contingencies, and the potential for technological and regulatory
developments. In addition, the impact of evolving programs, such as natural resource damage claims, industrial site reuse initiatives and state remediation programs creates further uncertainty of the
ultimate resolution of these environmental contingencies. We anticipate that the resolution of many contingencies, and in particular environmental contingencies, will occur over an extended period of
time. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>During
September 2010, our Lake Charles North and Plaquemine, Louisiana facilities each received a Consolidated Compliance Order and Notice of Potential Penalty, alleging violations of various
requirements of those facilities' air permits, based largely on self-reported permit deviations related to record-keeping violations. The Company has been negotiating a possible settlement of these
matters with LDEQ. Based upon a communication from LDEQ in September 2014, the Company now believes this matter may require the payment of a monetary sanction in excess of $100,000 but it does not
expect that the resolution of this matter will have a material adverse effect on its financial statements for any period. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>On
December&nbsp;20, 2013, a fire occurred at our PHH vinyl chloride monomer ("VCM") manufacturing plant in Lake Charles, Louisiana. As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, approximately 2,615 individuals
had filed lawsuits against the Company alleging personal injury or property damage related to the incident. We have not recorded an accrual in connection with any of these lawsuits because, at this
time, we are unable to reasonably determine whether any potential loss is probable or reasonably possible. In addition, we currently are unable to provide a reasonable estimate of the potential loss
or range of loss, if any, expected to result from this contingency. We are unable to make these determinations due to a number of variables, including without limitation, uncertainties related to:
(1)&nbsp;the fact that no written or oral discovery has been conducted by the Company in any of these lawsuits; (2)&nbsp;the procedural status and jurisdictions in which these lawsuits may be
adjudicated; (3)&nbsp;the parties' respective litigation strategies; (4)&nbsp;the fact that none of the complaints have alleged specific injuries or a specific amount of damages; (5)&nbsp;any
symptoms experienced by any of the plaintiffs, and whether there will be any reliable information, documentation or other discovery related thereto; (6)&nbsp;the pre-and-post fire medical or
physical condition of the plaintiffs, and whether there will be any reliable information, documentation or other discovery related thereto; and (7)&nbsp;the location of any plaintiff at the time of
the fire, and the duration of any exposure related thereto, and whether there will be any reliable information, documentation or other discovery related thereto. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Ability to Pay Dividends Under the ABL Revolver  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Under the ABL Revolver, cash dividend payments in an aggregate amount not to exceed $150&nbsp;million in any fiscal year may be made if both
borrowing availability under the ABL Revolver would have exceeded $75&nbsp;million at all times during the thirty days immediately preceding the dividend payment and our consolidated fixed charge
coverage ratio (as defined in the definitive documentation governing the ABL Revolver) is equal to or exceeds 1.00 to 1.00, each on a pro forma basis after giving effect to the proposed dividend
payment. In addition, under the ABL Revolver, additional cash dividend payments may be made if both borrowing availability under the ABL Revolver then exceeds $100&nbsp;million and our consolidated
fixed charge coverage ratio (as defined in the definitive documentation governing the ABL Revolver) is equal to or exceeds 1.10 to 1.00, each on a pro forma basis after giving effect to the proposed
cash dividend payment. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A HREF="#bg70001a_main_toc">Table of Contents</A> </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="do70001_item_7._management_s_discussio__ite03649"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_do70001_1"> </A></FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><B>  Item&nbsp;7.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>We are a leading North American manufacturer and international marketer of chemicals and building products. Our chlorovinyls and aromatics chemical
products are sold for further processing into a wide variety of end-use applications, including plastic pipe and pipe fittings, siding and window frames, bonding agents for wood products, high-quality
plastics, acrylic sheeting and coatings for wire and cable, paper, minerals, metals and water treatment industries. Our building products segment manufactures window and door profiles, trim, mouldings
and deck products, siding, pipe and pipe fittings. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Merger with PPG's Chemicals Business  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>On January&nbsp;28, 2013, we completed a series of transactions that resulted in our acquisition of substantially all of the assets and liabilities
of PPG Industries,&nbsp;Inc.'s ("PPG") business relating to the production of chlorine, caustic soda and related chemicals (the "Merged Business") through a merger between a subsidiary of PPG and a
subsidiary of the Company (the "Merger") and the related financings (collectively, the "Transactions"). The operations of the Merged Business are included in our chlorovinyls segment and are reflected
in our financial results from January&nbsp;28, 2013, the closing date of the Merger. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The
purchase price of the Merged Business was approximately $2.8&nbsp;billion and consisted of: (i)&nbsp;the issuance of approximately 35.2&nbsp;million shares of our common stock valued at
approximately $1.8&nbsp;billion; (ii)&nbsp;assumed debt of approximately $967.0&nbsp;million; and (iii)&nbsp;the assumption of other liabilities, including pension and OPEB obligations. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In
connection with the Merger, we incurred costs to attain synergies including plant reliability improvement initiatives, and transition costs such as consulting professionals' fees, information
technology implementation costs, relocation costs and severance costs, which management believed were necessary to realize approximately $140.0&nbsp;million of anticipated annualized cost synergies
within two years from the consummation of the Merger. As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, we incurred approximately $59.7&nbsp;million of such costs to attain Merger-related synergies, which includes
capitalized expenditures. In addition, we achieved $140.7&nbsp;million of annualized cost synergies within two years after the consummation of the Merger. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


<A NAME="a"></A>Results of Operations Overview  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Consolidated Overview  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, net sales totaled $4,568.7&nbsp;million, a decrease of 2&nbsp;percent compared to
$4,666.0&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. Operating
income was $134.1&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, compared to $370.8&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. Adjusted EBITDA was $436.3&nbsp;million
for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 compared to $672.0&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. In addition, the Company reported net income attributable to Axiall of
$46.3&nbsp;million, or $0.65 per diluted share for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, compared to net income attributable to Axiall of $165.3&nbsp;million, or $2.44 per diluted share for the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. Adjusted Net Income was $93.4&nbsp;million and Adjusted Earnings Per Share was $1.32 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, compared to Adjusted Net Income
of $266.1&nbsp;million and Adjusted Earnings Per Share of $3.93 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. See Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures in this Annual Report on
Form&nbsp;10-K. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>36</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<P style='font-family:times;page-break-before:always'></p>
<!-- ZEQ.=1,SEQ=36,EFW="2223048",CP="AXIALL CORPORATION",DN="1",CHK=366713,FOLIO='36',FILE='DISK105:[14ZDE1.14ZDE70001]DO70001A.;34',USER='DPERRY',CD='26-FEB-2015;20:24' -->
<A NAME="page_do70001_1_37"> </A>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A HREF="#bg70001a_main_toc">Table of Contents</A></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The
decrease in net sales for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 as compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 was primarily attributable to a $138.9&nbsp;million decrease in the net
sales of our aromatics segment which was due to decreased domestic demand for cumene and decreased export opportunities for phenol, partially offset by increases in the net sales of our chlorovinyls
and building products segments. The $12.9&nbsp;million increase in our chlorovinyls segment's net sales was partly due to the inclusion of twelve months of sales results from the Merged Business for
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 versus eleven months in the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, coupled with higher vinyl resin pricing during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. Net
sales in our building products segment increased $28.7&nbsp;million primarily due to higher sales volumes in the United States. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The
decreases in operating income, Adjusted EBITDA, net income attributable to Axiall and Adjusted Net Income, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, as compared to the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2013, were primarily attributable to: (i)&nbsp;lower operating rates and increased maintenance and operating costs due to several outages within our chlor-alkali operations, the
most significant of which included extended outages at our PHH vinyl chloride monomer ("VCM") manufacturing facility; (ii)&nbsp;lower electro-chemical unit ("ECU") values, especially with respect to
caustic soda pricing, resulting primarily from the addition of new production capacity in North America coupled with slower growth in the demand needed to absorb that capacity, partially offset by
higher pricing for our vinyl resins, VCM and chlorinated derivative products; (iii)&nbsp;a significant increase in our cost of natural gas and ethylene; and (iv)&nbsp;the decrease in domestic and
export demand for aromatics products made in North America due to new production capacity in Asia. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Chlorovinyls Business Overview  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our chlorovinyls segment produces a highly integrated chain of chlor-alkali and derivative products (chlorine, caustic soda, VCM, vinyl resins,
ethylene dichloride,
chlorinated solvents, calcium hypochlorite, muriatic acid and phosgene derivatives) and compound products (vinyl compounds and compound additives and plasticizers). As discussed further below, certain
highlights from our chlorovinyls segment results of operations for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 were as
follows:</FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Net sales totaled $2,930.2&nbsp;million and $2,917.3&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013,
respectively, increasing approximately $12.9&nbsp;million. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Operating income and Adjusted EBITDA decreased to $213.9&nbsp;million and $448.1&nbsp;million, respectively, during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2014 versus operating income and Adjusted EBITDA of $434.9&nbsp;million and $624.5&nbsp;million, respectively, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our
chlorovinyls segment is cyclical in nature and is affected by domestic and worldwide economic conditions. Cyclical price swings, driven by changes in supply and demand, can lead to significant
changes in the overall profitability of our chlorovinyls segment. The demand for our chlorovinyls products tends to reflect fluctuations in downstream markets that are affected by consumer spending
for durable and non-durable goods as well as construction. Global capacity also materially affects the prices of chlorovinyls products. Historically, in periods of high operating rates, prices rise
and margins increase and, as a result, new capacity is announced. Since world scale size plants are generally the most cost-competitive, new increases in capacity tend to be on a large scale and are
often undertaken by existing industry participants. Usually, as new capacity is added, prices decline until increases in demand improve operating rates and the new capacity is absorbed or, in some
instances, until less efficient producers withdraw capacity from the market. As the additional supply is absorbed, operating rates rise, prices increase and the cycle repeats. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>37</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<P style='font-family:times;page-break-before:always'></p>

<A NAME="page_do70001_1_38"> </A>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A HREF="#bg70001a_main_toc">Table of Contents</A></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In
addition, purchased raw materials and natural gas costs account for the majority of our cost of sales and can also have a material effect on our profitability and margins. Some of the primary raw
materials used in our chlorovinyls products, including ethylene, are crude oil and natural gas derivatives and therefore follow the oil and gas industry price trends. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Building Products Business Overview  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our building products segment consists of two primary product groups: (i)&nbsp;window and door profiles and trim, mouldings and deck products,
which include extruded vinyl window and door profiles, interior and exterior trim and mouldings products, as well as deck products; and (ii)&nbsp;outdoor building products, which includes siding,
pipe and pipe fittings. As discussed further below, certain highlights from our building products segment results of operations for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 compared to the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2013 were as follows:</FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Net sales totaled $878.6&nbsp;million and $849.9&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, respectively,
increasing 3&nbsp;percent. On a constant currency basis, net sales for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 increased by 7&nbsp;percent. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, our building products segment's geographical sales to the United States and Canada were
54&nbsp;percent and 45&nbsp;percent respectively, compared with 50&nbsp;percent and 49&nbsp;percent for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Operating income was $25.8&nbsp;million and Adjusted EBITDA was $67.7&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014
compared to operating income of $3.0&nbsp;million and Adjusted EBITDA of $70.7&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The
building products segment is impacted by changes in the North American home repair and remodeling sectors, as well as the new construction industry, which may be significantly affected by changes
in economic and other conditions such as gross domestic product levels, employment levels, demographic trends, consumer confidence, increases in interest rates and availability of consumer financing
for home repair and remodeling projects as well as the availability of financing for new home purchases. These factors can lower the demand for, and pricing of our products, while we may not be able
to reduce our costs by an equivalent amount. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Aromatics Business Overview  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our aromatics segment manufactures cumene products and phenol and acetone products (co-products made from cumene). As discussed further below,
certain highlights of our aromatics segment results of operations for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 were as
follows:</FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Net sales were $759.9&nbsp;million and $898.8&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, respectively,
decreasing 15&nbsp;percent in the aggregate and reflecting a 15&nbsp;percent decrease in cumene sales volume and a 23&nbsp;percent decrease in phenol and acetone sales volumes. </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Operating loss was $20.7&nbsp;million and Adjusted EBITDA was negative $18.5&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2014 compared to operating income of $29.1&nbsp;million and Adjusted EBITDA of $30.3&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In
our aromatics business, significant volatility in raw materials costs can decrease product margins as sales price increases sometimes lag raw materials cost increases. Product margins may also
suffer from </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 Compared With Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2013  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Consolidated Results  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Net sales.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, net sales totaled $4,568.7&nbsp;million, a decrease of 2&nbsp;percent compared to
$4,666.0&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The decrease in our consolidated net sales was primarily attributable to a $138.9&nbsp;million decrease in the net sales in our
aromatics segment partially offset by increases in the net sales of our chlorovinyls and building products segments. The decrease in our aromatics net sales was primarily due to decreased export
opportunities for phenol, which was caused primarily by recent additions of significant phenol production capacity in Asia. These same factors were also primarily responsible for the decrease in our
sales volume of cumene, as domestic producers of phenol manufactured less phenol, for which cumene is a raw material. Net sales in our chlorovinyls segment increased by $12.9&nbsp;million primarily
due to the inclusion of twelve months of sales results from the Merged Business for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 versus the inclusion of only eleven months of sales results from the Merged
Business for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, offset by: (i)&nbsp;lower operating rates and related sales volumes due to several outages within our chlor-alkali operations, the most
significant of which included extended outages at our PHH VCM manufacturing facility; and (ii)&nbsp;lower ECU values, for both chlorine and caustic soda pricing, caused primarily by the addition of
new production capacity in North America coupled with slower growth in the demand needed to absorb that capacity, partially offset by higher PVC and VCM prices. Net sales in our building products
segment increased by $28.7&nbsp;million primarily driven by a 17&nbsp;percent increase in sales volumes in the United States, partially offset by the impact of a stronger U.S. dollar against a
weaker Canadian dollar. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Gross margin percentage.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Total gross margin percentage decreased to 11&nbsp;percent for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from 16&nbsp;percent for the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. This decrease was principally due to: (i)&nbsp;lower operating rates and higher maintenance and operating costs due to several outages within our chlor-alkali
operations, the most significant of which included extended outages at our PHH VCM manufacturing facility; (ii)&nbsp;lower ECU values, for both chlorine and caustic soda pricing, caused primarily by
the factors discussed in the preceding paragraph, partially offset by higher pricing for our vinyl resins, VCM and chlorinated derivative products; (iii)&nbsp;higher natural gas and ethylene costs;
and (iv)&nbsp;the decrease in domestic and export demand for aromatics products made in North America due to
new production capacity in Asia. In December 2014, IHS reported that natural gas prices increased 20&nbsp;percent and ethylene prices increased by 3&nbsp;percent for the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2014 as compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. In 2013, the chlorovinyls segment's gross margin was negatively impacted by a $13.4&nbsp;million fair value inventory
acquisition accounting adjustment related to the Merged Business. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Selling, general and administrative expenses.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Selling, general and administrative expenses totaled $310.5&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2014, an increase of 4&nbsp;percent from $299.1&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. This increase was primarily due to the inclusion of twelve months of expenses from the
Merged Business during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, versus only eleven months for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, as well as increased amortization expense, professional fees and
promotional costs. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Transaction-related costs and other, net.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Transaction-related costs and other, net, increased 8&nbsp;percent to $38.4&nbsp;million during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $35.6&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. During 2014, our U.S. Pension Plans were amended to provide a one-time voluntary lump-sum
distribution offer to terminated vested participants and we recorded a settlement charge of $5.8&nbsp;million related to these costs. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, the company
recorded a curtailment gain of $15.5&nbsp;million related to certain pension plan amendments, partially offset by lower integration costs, costs to attain Merger-related synergies and deal-related
costs. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>40</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<P style='font-family:times;page-break-before:always'></p>

<A NAME="page_do70001_1_41"> </A>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Long-lived asset impairment charges, net.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Long-lived asset impairment charges, net decreased $18.4&nbsp;million to $17.6&nbsp;million during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $36.0&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company incurred approximately
$16.6&nbsp;million in long-lived and intangible asset impairment charges related to our phosgene derivatives product line that is classified as held-for-sale in our chlorovinyls segment. In 2013, we
recorded an impairment charge of $24.9&nbsp;million to write-down goodwill and other intangible assets in the window and door profiles reporting unit. The write-down was due primarily to the
prolonged downturn in the North American housing and construction markets, continued pricing declines, and the expected impact of those declines on projected cash flows on the window and door profiles
reporting unit. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Operating income.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating income was $134.1&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 compared to an operating income of $370.8&nbsp;million
for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The decrease in operating income was primarily a result of: (i)&nbsp;lower operating rates and increased maintenance and operating costs due to several
outages within our chlor-alkali operations, the most significant of which included extended outages at our PHH VCM manufacturing facility; (ii)&nbsp;lower ECU values for both chlorine and caustic
soda pricing, partially offset by higher pricing for our vinyl resins, VCM and chlorinated derivative products; (iii)&nbsp;higher natural gas and ethylene costs; and (iv)&nbsp;the decrease in
domestic and export demand for aromatics products made in North America due to new production capacity in Asia. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Interest expense.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest expense totaled $76.5&nbsp;million and $77.6&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, respectively. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Loss on redemption and other debt cost.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Loss on redemption and other debt cost resulted from the financing of the Transactions and financing fees associated with
the retirement of our 9&nbsp;percent notes in 2013, which included a $55.4&nbsp;million make-whole payment. There were no similar transactions or refinancing activities during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2014. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Gain on acquisition of controlling interest.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In January 2013, we acquired the Merged Business and the remaining 50&nbsp;percent interest of PHH that we did not
previously own. Prior to the Merger, we owned 50&nbsp;percent of PHH and accounted for our ownership interest as an equity method investment. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, we
recognized a gain of $25.9&nbsp;million as a result of remeasuring our prior equity interest in PHH held before the Merger in accordance with GAAP. We had no such gain during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2014. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Foreign currency exchange loss.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Foreign currency exchange loss totaled $0.6&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and was nominal for the year
ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The foreign currency exchange loss for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 is primarily due to the impact of a stronger U.S. dollar against a weaker Canadian
dollar. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Interest income.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest income totaled $0.7&nbsp;million and $1.0&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, respectively. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Provision for income</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2> taxes.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The provision for income taxes was $7.5&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, compared to a provision for income
taxes of $73.6&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The decrease was primarily due to a lower income before income taxes during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 compared
to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, as well as the release of uncertain tax positions for which the statute of limitations has expired, or effective settlement has occurred. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>41</FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our
effective income tax rates for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013 were 13.0&nbsp;percent and 30.5&nbsp;percent, respectively. The difference in the effective income tax rate as
compared to the United States statutory federal income tax rate in 2014 was primarily due to various permanent differences, including deductions for manufacturing activities, as well as a
$9.2&nbsp;million favorable impact from changes in uncertain tax positions. The difference in the effective income tax rate as compared to the United States statutory federal income tax rate in 2013
was primarily due to various permanent differences including deductions for manufacturing activities and a $2.7&nbsp;million favorable impact from changes in uncertain tax positions. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Chlorovinyls Segment  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Net sales.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net sales totaled $2,930.2&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, an increase of $12.9&nbsp;million versus net sales of
$2,917.3&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. Our overall net sales increase was primarily due to the inclusion of twelve months of sales results from the Merged Business for
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 versus the inclusion of only eleven months of sales results from the Merged Business for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, offset by: (i)&nbsp;lower
operating rates and related sales volumes due to several outages in our chlor-alkali operations, the most significant of which included extended outages at our PHH VCM manufacturing facility; and
(ii)&nbsp;lower ECU values for both chlorine and caustic soda pricing, caused primarily by the addition of new production capacity in North America coupled with slower growth in the demand needed to
absorb that capacity, partially offset by higher pricing for our vinyl resins, VCM and chlorinated derivative products. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Operating income.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating income decreased by $221.0&nbsp;million to $213.9&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from
$434.9&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The decrease was principally due to: (i)&nbsp;lower operating rates and increased maintenance and operating costs from several
outages within our chlor-alkali operations, the most significant of which included extended outages at our PHH VCM manufacturing facility; (ii)&nbsp;lower ECU values resulting primarily from the
reasons discussed above, partially offset by higher pricing for our vinyl resins, VCM and chlorinated derivative products; and (iii)&nbsp;increases in our cost of natural gas and ethylene. In
December 2014, IHS reported that industry natural gas prices increased 20&nbsp;percent and ethylene prices increased 3&nbsp;percent for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 compared to the year
ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, the segment's operating income was negatively impacted by a $13.4&nbsp;million fair value inventory acquisition
accounting adjustment related to the Merged Business and by $13.8&nbsp;million of costs to attain Merger-related synergies, which included $10.3&nbsp;million of plant reliability improvement
initiatives. Adjusted EBITDA decreased $176.4&nbsp;million to $448.1&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $624.5&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2013. That decrease was predominantly due to the same factors discussed above with respect to operating income, partially offset by the twelve full months of Adjusted EBITDA contributed by the Merged
Business in 2014 compared to eleven months in 2013. </FONT></P>

year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The net sales increase was primarily driven by a 17&nbsp;percent increase in sales volumes in the United States, partially offset by the impact of a stronger
U.S. dollar against a weaker Canadian dollar. On a constant currency basis, net sales increased by 7&nbsp;percent. For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, our building products segment's
geographical sales to the United States and Canada were 54&nbsp;percent and 45&nbsp;percent respectively, compared with 50&nbsp;percent and 49&nbsp;percent for the year ended

Aromatics Segment  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Net sales.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net sales were $759.9&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, a decrease of 15&nbsp;percent versus $898.8&nbsp;million for the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. The net sales decrease primarily resulted from a 15&nbsp;percent decrease in cumene sales volume and a 23&nbsp;percent decrease in phenol and acetone sales
volumes. The decrease in our sales volume of phenol is primarily due to a significant decline in export demand for phenol produced in the United States, which is primarily the result of the recent
addition of a significant amount of new phenol production capacity in Asia. These same factors are also primarily responsible for the decrease in our sales volume of cumene. Specifically, domestic
producers of phenol are manufacturing less phenol, for which cumene is a raw material, in response to the decline in export demand for phenol. Accordingly, those domestic producers, some of which have
historically been our customers, have required significantly less cumene. In addition, the decline in our cumene sales volume has been caused in part by certain of our customers purchasing less cumene
from us on a contracted basis. We expect these lower levels of phenol sales volumes to continue in 2015. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Operating income (loss).</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Operating loss was $20.7&nbsp;million and operating income was $29.1&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and
2013, respectively. Our operating rates for the aromatics segment were lower in the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, versus the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 and were lower than the industry
operating rates for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, as reported in the December 2014 IHS publication. The $49.8&nbsp;million decrease in operating income and our lower operating rates were
due primarily to (i)&nbsp;the overall weakening of the domestic and international aromatics markets; (ii)&nbsp;a $11.9&nbsp;million inventory holding loss due to a significant decline in raw
material costs; and (iii)&nbsp;a $9.2&nbsp;million lower-of-cost or market adjustment for inventory during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2014. The Adjusted EBITDA decrease of $48.8&nbsp;million to negative $18.5&nbsp;million for the year ending December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $30.3&nbsp;million for the year
ending December&nbsp;31, 2013 was principally due to lower domestic and export sales volumes, the inventory holding loss due to a significant decline in raw material costs, and the lower of cost or
market inventory adjustment, as well as the factors discussed in the preceding paragraph. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


<A NAME="c"></A>Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Axiall has supplemented its financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP that are set forth in this Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K (the
"Financial Statements") with four non-GAAP financial measures: (i)&nbsp;Adjusted Net Income; (ii)&nbsp;Adjusted Earnings Per Share; (iii)&nbsp;Adjusted EBITDA; and (iv)&nbsp;building products
net sales on a constant currency basis. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Adjusted
Net Income is defined as net income attributable to Axiall excluding adjustments for tax effected cash and non-cash restructuring charges and certain other charges, if any, related to
financial restructuring and business improvement initiatives, gains or losses on redemption and other debt costs, and sales of certain assets, certain acquisition accounting and certain non-income tax
reserve adjustments, professional fees related to a previously disclosed and withdrawn unsolicited offer and the Merger, costs to attain Merger-related synergies, goodwill, intangible assets, and
other long-lived asset impairments. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Adjusted
Earnings Per Share is calculated using Adjusted Net Income rather than consolidated net income calculated in accordance with GAAP. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Adjusted
EBITDA is defined as Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization, cash and non-cash restructuring charges and certain other charges, if any, related to financial
restructuring and business improvement initiatives, gains or losses on redemption and other debt costs, and sales of certain assets, certain acquisition accounting and certain non-income tax reserve
adjustments, professional fees related to a previously disclosed and withdrawn unsolicited offer and the Merger, costs to attain Merger-related synergies, goodwill, intangible assets, other long-lived
asset impairments, certain pension and other post-retirement plan curtailment gains and settlement losses and interest expense related to the lease-financing transaction discussed in Note&nbsp;8 to
this Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Axiall
has supplemented the financial statements with Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Earnings Per Share because investors commonly use financial measures such as Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted
Earnings Per Share as a component of performance and valuation analysis for companies, such as Axiall, that recently have engaged in transactions that result in non-recurring pre-tax charges or
benefits that have a significant impact on the calculation of consolidated net income pursuant to GAAP, in order to approximate the amount of net income that such a company would have achieved absent
those non-recurring, transaction-related charges or benefits. In addition, Axiall has supplemented the Financial Statements with Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Earnings Per Share because we believe
these financial measures will be helpful to investors in approximating what our net income would have </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>been
absent the impact of certain non-recurring, pre-tax charges and benefits related to the Merger, the Company's issuance of its 4.875 Notes and the tender offer for, and related redemption of its
9&nbsp;percent notes. We have supplemented the financial statements with Adjusted EBITDA because investors commonly use Adjusted EBITDA as a main component of valuation analysis of cyclical
companies such as Axiall. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In
addition, we may compare certain financial information, including building products net sales, on a constant currency basis. We present such information to provide a framework for investors to
assess how our underlying businesses performed, excluding the effect of foreign currency rate fluctuations, primarily fluctuations in the Canadian dollar. To present this information, current and
comparative prior period financial information for certain businesses reporting in currencies other than United States dollars are converted into United States dollars at the average exchange rate in
effect during the period, rather than the average exchange rates in effect during the respective periods. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Adjusted
Earnings Per Share, Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted EBITDA and building products net sales on a constant currency basis, are not measurements of financial performance under GAAP and should not
be considered as an alternative to net income, GAAP diluted earnings per share or net sales, as a measure of performance or to cash provided by operating activities as a measure of liquidity. In
addition, our calculation of Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted Earnings Per Share, Adjusted EBITDA and building products net sales on a constant currency basis, may be different from the calculations used
by other companies and, therefore, comparability may be limited. Reconciliations of these non-GAAP financial measures to the most comparable GAAP measures are presented in the tables set forth below. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Operating Activities.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In the consolidated statements of cash flows, changes in operating assets and liabilities are presented excluding the effects of changes in
foreign currency, non-cash transactions and the effects of acquisitions and divestitures. Accordingly, the amounts in the consolidated statements of cash flows differ from changes in the operating
assets and liabilities that are presented in the consolidated balance sheets. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Net
working capital for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012 was $621.0&nbsp;million, $625.4&nbsp;million, and $488.3&nbsp;million, respectively. Cash flows from operating
activities decreased $34.6&nbsp;million for the year ending December&nbsp;31, 2014 and increased $94.5&nbsp;million and $43.8&nbsp;million during the years ending December&nbsp;31, 2013 and
2012, respectively. The changes in our cash flows provided by operating activities were primarily driven by our net operating results coupled with changes in our operating working capital. The changes
in our operating assets and liabilities and the impact of </FONT></P>

 <DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2><SUP>(1)</SUP></FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>An
increase in assets increases our operating working capital which decreases operating cash flows and an increase in liabilities decreases
our operating working capital and increases our operating cash flows. Conversely, a decrease in assets decreases our operating working capital which increases our operating cash flows and a decrease
in liabilities increases our operating working capital which decreases our operating cash flows. </FONT></DD></DL>
 </DIV>
 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Investing Activities.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Cash used in investing activities increased $68.9&nbsp;million and $82.9&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and
2013, respectively, and decreased $79.8&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012. Capital expenditures increased $14.4&nbsp;million, $115.8&nbsp;million and $13.9&nbsp;million
for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012, respectively. In 2014, the increase in investing activities was primarily due to capital expenditures associated with the Merged Business,
including repairs associated with the December 2013 fire at our PHH VCM manufacturing facility in Lake Charles, Louisiana (net of $3.9&nbsp;million of proceeds pertaining to a settlement with our
insurers related to that event), and acquisitions, net of cash acquired, of $6.1&nbsp;million, offset by proceeds of $8.1&nbsp;million, primarily from government grants and the sale of assets. The
increase in 2013 was primarily due to the operations acquired in the Merger, offset by $45.1&nbsp;million of cash acquired with the Merged Business which included a $22.0&nbsp;million payment that
PPG made to us in November 2013 for the net working capital settlement in connection with the Merger and $11.4&nbsp;million in proceeds from the sale of assets. During 2012, our capital investments
were reduced by proceeds from the sale of assets totaling $23.6&nbsp;million, primarily relating to the sale of our on-site air separation unit at our Plaquemine, Louisiana facility for
$18.0&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>On
January&nbsp;28, 2013, we completed the Merger and acquired the Merged Business. The purchase price for the Merged Business was approximately $2.8&nbsp;billion and consisted of: (i)&nbsp;the
issuance of approximately 35.2&nbsp;million shares of our common stock valued at approximately $1.8&nbsp;billion; (ii)&nbsp;the assumed debt of approximately $967.0&nbsp;million; and
(iii)&nbsp;the assumption of certain other liabilities including pension and OPEB obligations. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>We
incurred maintenance expense for our production facilities of $329.9&nbsp;million, $312.4&nbsp;million and $157.3&nbsp;million during the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012,
respectively, with the increases in 2014 and 2013 primarily due to the operations acquired in the Merger. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Financing Activities.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Cash used in financing activities decreased $140.9&nbsp;million in 2014, increased $152.4&nbsp;million in 2013 and decreased
$21.8&nbsp;million in 2012. In 2014, our financing activities included
$45.0&nbsp;million for dividend payments and $10.0&nbsp;million related to deferred acquisition payments to PPG. In 2013, our financing activities included the issuance and redemption of long-term
debt as described in the preceding paragraphs, $98.1&nbsp;million in make-whole and other fees related to the Transactions and $22.2&nbsp;million in dividend payments. During 2012, cash used in
financing activities primarily consisted of the early redemption of $50.0&nbsp;million principal amount of our 9&nbsp;percent notes, plus early redemption fees and $8.3&nbsp;million related to
our reinstatement of paying dividends on outstanding common stock in the aggregate amount of $0.24 per share during 2012. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


4.625 Notes  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The Company and certain of its subsidiaries guarantee $688.0&nbsp;million aggregate principal amount of senior unsecured notes due 2021 bearing
interest at a rate of 4.625&nbsp;percent per annum (the "4.625 Notes") that were issued by Eagle Spinco&nbsp;Inc., ("Spinco"). Interest payments on the 4.625 Notes commenced on August&nbsp;15,
2013 and interest is payable semi-annually in arrears on February&nbsp;15 and August&nbsp;15 of each year. The 4.625 Notes are fully and unconditionally guaranteed, jointly and severally, on a
senior unsecured basis by the Company and by the Company's existing and future domestic subsidiaries, other than certain excluded subsidiaries. The proceeds from the 4.625 Notes retired a
$688.0&nbsp;million bridge loan for which we incurred $11.0&nbsp;million of costs for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, related to financing fees that are included in "Loss on redemption
and other debt costs" in our consolidated statements of operations. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


4.875 Notes  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>On February&nbsp;1, 2013, Axiall Corporation issued $450.0&nbsp;million in aggregate principal amount of senior unsecured notes due 2023 which
bear interest at a rate of 4.875&nbsp;percent per annum (the "4.875 Notes"). Interest payments on the 4.875 Notes commenced on May&nbsp;15, 2013 and interest is payable semi-annually in arrears on
May&nbsp;15 and November&nbsp;15 of each year. The 4.875 Notes are fully and unconditionally guaranteed, jointly and severally, on a senior unsecured basis by each of our existing and future
domestic subsidiaries, other than certain excluded subsidiaries. The net proceeds from the offering of the 4.875 Notes, together with cash on hand, funded the repurchase of our 9&nbsp;percent senior
secured notes due 2017 (the "9&nbsp;percent notes") in a tender offer and related consent solicitation (the "Tender Offer") for an aggregate tender price of $502.3&nbsp;million, including a make
whole payment of $55.4&nbsp;million. We accounted for the repurchase of the 9&nbsp;percent notes as an extinguishment and </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>53</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<P style='font-family:times;page-break-before:always'></p>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>expensed
approximately $8.5&nbsp;million of deferred financing fees and incurred charges of $2.2&nbsp;million associated with the Tender Offer during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Term Loan  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, the Company also guaranteed a $279.0&nbsp;million term loan due 2017 made to Spinco (the "Term
Loan"). The Term Loan bears interest at a rate equal to (at the Company's election): (i)&nbsp;the Base Rate (as defined in the Term Loan agreement and subject to a 2&nbsp;percent floor) plus
1.50&nbsp;percent per annum; or (ii)&nbsp;the reserve adjusted Eurodollar Rate (as defined in the Term Loan agreement and subject to a 1&nbsp;percent floor) plus 2.50&nbsp;percent per annum.
As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, outstanding borrowings under the Company's Term Loan had a stated interest rate of 3.50&nbsp;percent per annum and an effective interest rate, inclusive of
amortization of deferred debt issuance cost, of approximately 3.9&nbsp;percent. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Obligations
under the Term Loan are fully and unconditionally guaranteed, on a senior secured basis, by the Company and its existing and future domestic subsidiaries, other than certain excluded
subsidiaries and are secured by all the assets of the Company and the subsidiary guarantors. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>During
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, we repaid approximately $81.8&nbsp;million of the outstanding balance of the Term Loan. In connection with the repayment, we expensed
$1.4&nbsp;million of deferred financing fees, which is included in "Loss on redemption and other debt costs" in our consolidated statements of operations. During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2014, we repaid an additional $2.8&nbsp;million of the outstanding balance of our Term Loan in accordance with the contractual terms of our agreement. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


ABL Revolver  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In December 2014, the Company amended and restated its asset-based revolving credit facility (the "ABL Revolver") to, among other things, increase
the commitments under the ABL Revolver from $500.0&nbsp;million to $600.0&nbsp;million and extend the maturity date to December&nbsp;17, 2019. At the Company's election, with respect to
borrowings in the United States under the ABL
Revolver, the borrowings bear interest at a rate equal to either: (i)&nbsp;the higher of certain index rates; or (ii)&nbsp;three-month London Interbank Offered Rate ("LIBOR"), plus an applicable
margin. At the election of the Company, with respect to borrowings in Canada under the ABL Revolver, the borrowings will bear interest at a rate equal to either: (i)&nbsp;the higher of certain index
rates; or (ii)&nbsp;three-month LIBOR, if available, in each case, plus an applicable margin. The applicable margin for borrowings under the ABL Revolver will be 0.50&nbsp;percent per annum for
base rate and index loans and 1.50&nbsp;percent per annum for LIBOR margin loans, provided that if the Company has not received a corporate family credit rating of at least Ba3 from Moody's and BB-
from S&amp;P, the applicable margin will range from 0.5&nbsp;percent to 1.0&nbsp;percent, with respect to base rate and index loans and 1.5&nbsp;percent to 2.0&nbsp;percent with respect to LIBOR
margin loans, depending on the utilization percentages set forth in the ABL Revolver. As of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, we had no outstanding balance on our ABL Revolver. As of
December&nbsp;31, 2014, our availability under the ABL Revolver was approximately $429.8&nbsp;million, net of outstanding letters of credit totaling $82.3&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The
ABL Revolver is fully and unconditionally guaranteed, on a senior secured basis, by each of the Company's existing and subsequently acquired or organized direct or indirect domestic subsidiaries,
other than certain excluded subsidiaries. Canadian borrowing obligations under the ABL Revolver are unconditionally guaranteed by each of the Company's existing and subsequently acquired or organized
direct or indirect domestic and Canadian subsidiaries, other than certain excluded subsidiaries. All obligations under the ABL Revolver, and the guarantees of those obligations, are secured, subject
to </FONT></P>

exceptions, by substantially all of the Company's assets and the assets of the subsidiary guarantors. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The
ABL Revolver, the Term Loan agreement and the indentures governing the 4.625 Notes and the 4.875 Notes each contain customary covenants, including certain restrictions on the Company and its
subsidiaries ability to pay dividends and repurchase shares of Company stock. These covenants are subject to certain exceptions and qualifications. Under the ABL Revolver, dividend payments and
repurchases of our common stock in an aggregate amount not to exceed $150&nbsp;million in any fiscal year may be made if both borrowing availability under the ABL Revolver would have exceeded
$75&nbsp;million at all times during the thirty days immediately preceding any such restricted payment and our consolidated fixed charge coverage ratio (as defined in the ABL Revolver) is equal to
or exceeds 1.00 to 1.00, each on a pro forma basis after giving effect to any such proposed restricted payment. In addition, under the ABL Revolver, additional cash dividend payments may be made if
both borrowing availability under the ABL Revolver then exceeds $100&nbsp;million and our consolidated fixed charge coverage ratio (as defined in the ABL Revolver) is equal to or exceeds 1.10 to
1.00, each on a pro forma basis after giving effect to the proposed cash dividend payment. As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, we were in compliance with the covenants under the ABL Revolver, the Term
Loan agreement and the indentures governing the 4.625 Notes and 4.875 Notes. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In
connection with the issuance of each of the 4.625 Notes and 4.875 Notes, we entered into a registration rights agreement, pursuant to which we and the guarantors agreed to use our commercially
reasonable efforts to file an exchange offer registration statement registering the 4.625 Notes and 4.875 Notes. On June&nbsp;27, 2014, the Company completed the exchange offer registering the 4.625
Notes and 4.875 Notes with the SEC in satisfaction of the terms of these agreements. </FONT></P>

under the ABL Revolver, if any, were at variable interest rates. </FONT></P>

Subsequent Events  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>On February&nbsp;27, 2015, Axiall Holdco,&nbsp;Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company ("Axiall Holdco"), entered into a credit agreement
with a syndicate of financial institutions (the "Term Loan Agreement") for a new $250&nbsp;million term loan facility (the "New Term Loan Facility") in order to refinance the principal amount
outstanding under Spinco's existing Term Loan Facility, pay related fees and expenses, and for general corporate purposes. Obligations under the New Term Loan Facility are fully and unconditionally
guaranteed, on a senior secured basis, by the Company and by each of the Company's existing and future wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries, other than certain excluded subsidiaries. The obligations
under the New Term Loan Facility are secured by substantially all of the assets of Axiall Holdco, the Company and the subsidiary guarantors. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Borrowings
under the New Term Loan are expected to mature on the seventh anniversary of the closing date. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>At
the election of Axiall Holdco, the New Term Loan Facility bears interest at a rate equal to: (i)&nbsp;the Base Rate (as defined in the Term Loan Agreement) plus 1.50&nbsp;percent per annum; or
(ii)&nbsp;LIBOR (as defined in the Term Loan Agreement) plus 3.25&nbsp;percent per annum; provided that at no time will the Base Rate be deemed to be less than 2.00&nbsp;percent per annum or
LIBOR be deemed to be less than 0.75&nbsp;percent per annum. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The
Term Loan Agreement contains customary covenants (subject to exceptions), including certain restrictions on the Company and its subsidiaries to pay dividends. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Lease Financing Obligation  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>As of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, we had a lease financing obligation of $94.2&nbsp;million and $104.7&nbsp;million, respectively. The
change from the December&nbsp;31, 2013 balance is due to a one-time $2.3&nbsp;million payment and the change in the Canadian dollar exchange rate as of
December&nbsp;31, 2014. The lease financing obligation is the result of the sale and concurrent leaseback of certain land and buildings in Canada in 2007 for a term of ten years. In connection with
this transaction, a collateralized letter of credit was issued in favor of the buyer-lessor. That factor and certain other terms and conditions resulted in the transaction being recorded as a
financing transaction rather than a sale for GAAP purposes. As a result, the land, building and related accounts continue to be recognized in the consolidated balance sheets. The amount of the
collateralized letter of credit was $1.6&nbsp;million and $3.8&nbsp;million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, respectively. The collateralized letter of credit expired on February&nbsp;2,
2015 and is no longer required. We are not obligated to repay the lease financing obligation amount of $94.2&nbsp;million. Our obligation is for the future minimum lease payments under the terms of
the related lease agreements. The future minimum lease payments under the terms of the related lease agreements as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 are $5.5&nbsp;million in 2015, $5.5&nbsp;million in
2016 and $1.4&nbsp;million in 2017, the final year of the lease agreements. The change in the future minimum lease payments from such amounts disclosed as of December&nbsp;31, 2013 is due to the
one-time $2.3&nbsp;million payment, current period lease payments and the change in the Canadian dollar exchange rate as of December&nbsp;31, 2014. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><I>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Management believes, based on current and projected levels of operations and conditions in our markets and cash flow from operations, together with our cash and cash
equivalents on hand and the availability to borrow under our ABL Revolver, we have adequate funding for the foreseeable future to make required payments of interest on our debt, fund our operating
needs, working capital and capital expenditure requirements, comply with the financial ratios in our debt agreements, and make any required prepayments of principal under our debt agreements. As of
February&nbsp;27, 2015, we have no significant required payments of principal on our debt until December 2019. To the extent our cash flow and liquidity exceeds the levels necessary for us to make
required payments on our debt, fund our working capital and capital expenditure requirements and comply with our ABL Revolver, we may use the excess liquidity to further grow our business through
investments or acquisitions, payment of dividends and/or to reduce our debt. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Purchase obligations.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Purchase obligations primarily include agreements to purchase goods or services that are enforceable and legally binding and that specify all
significant terms. We have certain long-term raw material supply contracts and energy purchase agreements with various terms extending through 2026. These commitments are designed to assure sources of
supply for our normal requirements. Amounts are based upon contractual raw material volumes and market rates as of December&nbsp;31, 2014. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Long-term debt, principal.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Long-term debt principal obligations are listed in the table above based on the contractual due dates. On February&nbsp;27, 2015, we
entered into a new $250&nbsp;million term loan facility, which matures on February&nbsp;27, 2022, to refinance our existing term loan facility, pay related fees and expenses, and for general
corporate purposes. See Note&nbsp;9 of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Long-term debt, interest.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Long-term debt interest payments set forth in the table above are based on our contractual rates, or in the case of variable interest
rate obligations, the weighted average interest rates as of December&nbsp;31, 2014. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Lease financing obligations.</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We lease land and buildings for certain of our Canadian manufacturing facilities under leases with varying maturities through the year
2017. </FONT></P>

<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Outlook  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>We expect our first quarter 2015 financial results to be negatively impacted by several factors including: (i) above average maintenance expenses and
reduced operating rates due to planned outages in our VCM, PVC, chlor-alkali and chlorinated derivatives operations; and (ii) a continued weak Canadian dollar, as compared to a stronger U.S. dollar,
which we expect to negatively impact the earnings of our Building Products segment. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Prices
for both chlorine and caustic soda have declined in the last several quarters. Although demand for chlorine has been solid in January and February 2015, we believe the near-term direction of
caustic prices is uncertain and ultimately will be determined by the pace at which global demand absorbs the chlor-alkali manufacturing capacity added to North America in early 2014. In addition, PVC
price declines accelerated in January 2015, and current margins for PVC are well below the average PVC margin achieved in the quarter ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. Taking all of these factors into
consideration, we believe expectations for margins in both ECU products and PVC will not become clear before the second quarter of 2015. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Over
the longer term, we expect to sustain our operations at the improved levels we realized in the second half of 2014. In addition, we believe ECU values will be driven higher by the strength of
domestic demand and improved export volumes for ECU products. We believe we are also well positioned to take advantage of a number of macro-economic and industry trends. In particular, we </FONT></P>

Inflation  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The most significant component of our cost of sales is raw materials, which include basic oil-based commodities and natural gas or derivatives
thereof. The costs of raw materials and natural gas are based primarily on market forces and have not been significantly affected by inflation. Inflation has not had a material impact on our sales or
income from operations. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


New Accounting Pronouncements  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In January 2015, the Financial Accounting Standards Board ("FASB") issued Accounting Standards Update ("ASU" or "Update)
2015-01&#151;</FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Extraordinary and Unusual Items (Subtopic 225-20</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>). The Update eliminates from GAAP the concept of extraordinary items as part of
FASB's initiative to reduce the complexity in current accounting standards. Previous GAAP guidance required an entity to separately classify, present, and disclose extraordinary events and
transactions. An event or transaction was presumed to be both ordinary and usual unless evidence clearly supported classification as an extraordinary item. However, the concept of extraordinary items
caused uncertainty in practice because it was unclear as to when an item should be considered both unusual and infrequent and it was extremely rare in practice for a transaction or event to meet the
classification requirement of an extraordinary item. Going forward, items that would have met the definition of extraordinary items will be treated in a similar manner as unusual and infrequent items.
The amendments in this Update are effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2015 and early adoption is permitted. We have adopted the amendments in this Update and
there was no material impact on our consolidated financial statements. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In
June 2014, FASB issued ASU 2014-12&#151;Compensation&#151;Stock Compensation (Topic 718). Under this Update: </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Accounting for Share-Based Payments When the Terms
of an Award Provide That a Performance Target Could Be Achieved after the Requisite Service Period</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2> (a consensus of the FASB Emerging Issues Task Force), a performance target
that affects vesting, and that could be achieved after the requisite service period, would be treated as a performance condition. GAAP did not address these issues. The Update states that a reporting
entity should apply existing guidance in Topic 718 to account for awards with performance conditions that affect the vesting of such awards. As such, the performance target should not be reflected in
estimating the grant-date fair value of the award. Compensation cost should be recognized in the period in which it becomes probable that the performance target will be achieved and should represent
the compensation cost attributable to the periods for which the requisite service has already been rendered. If the performance target becomes probable of being achieved before the end of the
requisite service period, the remaining unrecognized compensation cost should be recognized prospectively over the remaining requisite service period. The total amount of compensation cost recognized
during and after the requisite service period should reflect the number of awards that are expected to vest and should be adjusted to reflect those awards that ultimately vest. The requisite service
period ends when the employee can cease rendering service and still be eligible to vest in the award if the performance target is achieved. The stated vesting period </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>(which
includes the period in which the performance target could be achieved) may differ from the requisite service period. The amendments in this Update are effective for annual reporting periods
beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2015. Earlier adoption is permitted. We are evaluating the amendments in this Update and have not yet determined the impact on our consolidated financial
statements. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In
May 2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-09, </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Revenue from Contracts with Customers</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. The Update outlines a single, comprehensive model for entities to use
in accounting for revenue arising from contracts with customers and supersedes most current revenue recognition guidance issued by the FASB, including industry specific guidance. The Update provides
accounting guidance for all revenue arising from contracts with customers and affects all entities that enter into contracts with customers to provide goods and services. The guidance also provides a
model for the measurement and recognition of gains and losses on the sale of certain nonfinancial assets, such as property and equipment, including real estate. The Update is effective for annual
reporting periods, including interim reporting periods within those periods, beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2016. The new standard must be adopted using either a full retrospective approach for
all periods presented in the period of adoption or a modified retrospective approach. The modified retrospective approach requires that the new standard be applied to all new and existing contracts as
of the date of adoption, with a cumulative catch-up adjustment recorded to the opening balance of retained earnings at the effective date for existing contracts that still require performance by the
entity. Under the modified retrospective approach, amounts reported prior to the date of adoption will be presented under existing guidance. The Update also requires entities to disclose both
quantitative and qualitative information to enable users of the financial statements to understand the nature, amount, timing, and uncertainty of revenue and cash flows arising from contracts with
customers. We have not yet determined the impact of adopting the standard on our consolidated financial statements, nor have we determined whether we will utilize the full retrospective or modified
retrospective approach. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In
April 2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-08&#151;</FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Reporting Discontinued Operations and Disclosures of Disposals of Components of an Entity</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. The
amendments in this Update change the requirements for reporting discontinued operations in Subtopics 205 (Presentation of Financial Statements) and 360 (Property, Plant, and Equipment). The Update
changes the criteria for reporting discontinued operations and enhances the FASB's convergence with International Accounting Standards. The Update improves the definition of discontinued operations by
limiting discontinued operations reporting specifically to the disposal of a component or a group of components of an entity that results in a strategic shift that has (or will have) a major effect on
an entity's operations and financial results when certain criteria are met. The Update raises the threshold for disposals to qualify as discontinued operations and expands the disclosure requirements
for discontinued operations and certain other disposals that do not qualify as discontinued operations. The amendments in this Update are effective for annual periods beginning on or after
December&nbsp;15, 2014, and interim periods within that year. We have adopted the amendments in this Update and there was no material impact on our consolidated financial statements. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In
July 2013, the FASB issued ASU 2013-11, Income Taxes (Topic 740): </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Presentation of an Unrecognized Tax Benefit When a Net Operating Loss Carryforward, a Similar Tax Loss, or
a Tax Credit Carryforward Exists</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. Prior to this Update, GAAP did not include explicit guidance on the financial statement presentation of an unrecognized tax benefit when a net
operating loss carryforward, a similar tax loss, or a tax credit carryforward existed. The Update provides that a liability related to an unrecognized tax benefit would be offset against a deferred
tax asset for a net operating loss carryforward, a similar tax loss or a tax credit carryforward if such settlement is required or expected in the event the uncertain tax position is disallowed. In
that case, the liability associated with the unrecognized tax benefit is presented in the financial statements as a reduction to the related deferred tax asset for a net operating loss carryforward, a
similar tax loss or a tax credit carryforward. In situations in which a net operating </FONT></P>
